security_audit.summary: SKILL.md is a documentation-only Better Auth guide with no executable scripts or prompt injection evidence. The confirmed risks are setup commands that can run npm or npx tooling and modify project, database, or AI tool configuration.

remediation.issue: Setup commands can execute package tooling
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npm install or npx commands, and prefer pinned package or CLI versions when possible.

remediation.issue: CLI migration and generation commands can modify project state
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review pending schema and file changes before applying migrations or generated adapter files.

remediation.issue: MCP configuration command changes an AI tool setup
remediation.suggestion: Mark MCP setup as optional and require explicit consent before modifying Cursor or other AI tool configuration.

content.value_statement: Better Auth setup can break when server, client, database, and session options are configured separately. This skill gives concise setup guidance and security checks for TypeScript authentication projects.
actual_capabilities: Outline the Better Auth setup workflow for server config, routes, clients, and environment variables.
Summarize database adapter choices for direct connections, Prisma, Drizzle, and MongoDB.
Explain session storage, cookie cache modes, expiration, and database persistence options.
Identify security-sensitive settings such as secure cookies, CSRF checks, origin checks, and rate limits.
Guide plugin imports, client plugin placement, and schema regeneration after plugin changes.
Point users to Better Auth documentation, options reference, and source links for current details.
limitations: It is a concise guide, not a full replacement for the official Better Auth documentation.
It does not validate an application database schema or provider credentials by itself.
It does not perform a threat model for each production deployment.
Latest API details still need verification against official Better Auth resources.

use_cases.title: Set Up Authentication
use_cases.description: Add Better Auth to a TypeScript application with required server, route, database, and client pieces.

use_cases.title: Review Session Behavior
use_cases.description: Check session storage, cookie cache strategy, expiration, and database persistence before release.

use_cases.title: Plan Plugin Changes
use_cases.description: Choose Better Auth plugins, place client plugins correctly, and rerun schema generation when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Setup Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new TypeScript app.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am adding Better Auth to a TypeScript app. Give me the setup order for auth.ts, routes, environment variables, database, and client usage.

prompt_templates.title: Add Sign-In Methods
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate configuration for email and social auth.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure Better Auth for email and password plus one social provider. Include required environment variables and security checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Sessions And Cookies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Better Auth session plan. Compare database sessions, secondary storage, cookie cache modes, expiration, and secure cookie settings.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit a Better Auth production configuration for risky options, missing rate limits, weak origin settings, plugin schema needs, and migration concerns.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for the minimum Better Auth setup steps.
output_examples.output: A short ordered checklist covering package setup, required secrets, auth configuration, route handler, migration step, and health verification.

output_examples.input: A backend engineer asks whether sessions should use secondary storage or the database.
output_examples.output: A comparison of storage behavior, persistence tradeoffs, logout effects, and cookie cache limits for the planned deployment.

output_examples.input: A team asks which security options need review before launch.
output_examples.output: A focused review list for secure cookies, CSRF protection, origin checks, trusted origins, rate limiting, and proxy IP headers.

best_practices: Keep Better Auth secrets in environment variables and use at least 32 characters for the secret value.
Rerun Better Auth schema generation or migrations after adding or changing plugins.
Review secure cookies, origin checks, CSRF behavior, and rate limits before production release.
anti_patterns: Do not disable CSRF or origin checks unless a reviewed architecture requires it.
Do not use database table names when Better Auth expects adapter model names.
Do not assume custom session fields are always present in cookie cache data.

faq.question: Does this skill write Better Auth code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides configuration guidance and review prompts. The agent can draft code only when the user asks for implementation.

faq.question: Does it support multiple frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide references server routes and Better Auth clients for vanilla, React, Vue, Svelte, and Solid projects.

faq.question: Can it help with database adapters?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers direct database connections and ORM adapters for Prisma, Drizzle, and MongoDB.

faq.question: Can it review security settings?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights secure cookies, CSRF checks, origin checks, trusted origins, proxy headers, and rate limiting.

faq.question: Does it replace the official documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a compact workflow guide and should be checked against official Better Auth documentation for current API details.

faq.question: Are command examples run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Package, migration, generation, and MCP commands should run only after explicit user approval.
